data.name: Ghiyath
data.long_meaning: Ghiyath is a name derived from the Arabic root 'gh-y-th'. It means to help, aid, assist, and support. In Islamic history, Ghiyath was a title given to Prophet Ibrahim (AS) for his unwavering faith in Allah and his ability to guide and support his people.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of support and guidance in times of need.
data.numerology_meaning: People with the name Ghiyath are adaptable, resourceful, and versatile. They are deeply empathetic and able to sense the emotions of others, making them natural healers and They have a strong sense of self-discipline and are highly intelligent.

in_arabic.name: غيث
in_arabic.meaning: الغيثُ: المطر المذيب، وهو المطر الذى يأتي بعد الحاجة
in_arabic.long_meaning: الغيثُ: المطر المذيب، وهو المطر الذى يأتي بعد الحاجة والجفاف، وهو من أسماء الله الحسنة، ويُستخدَم فى القرآن الكريم فى سورة الشورى: {وَلَوْ لَا دُعَاؤُهُ غَيْرَ الْجِزْعِ لَمَسَحَهُ الظَلاَمُ} [الشورى:10].

in_urdu.name: غیاث
in_urdu.meaning: غیاث کے معنی ہیں چھاونی والا مطر، پانی، بارش، برسات، بہتا ہوا پانی، دھوپ اور ہوا
in_urdu.long_meaning: غیاث کے معنی ہیں چھاونی والا مطر، پانی، بارش، برسات، بہتا ہوا پانی، دھوپ اور ہوا، اس نام کا آغاز ہجری سال 10ھ سے ہوا، اس نام کے معنی ہے مگر جس کا معنی ہے چھاونی والا مطر، اس نام کی وجہ تسمیہ اس لیے ہے کہ غیاث کے نام والے بزرگوں کو اللہ تعالیٰ نے بارش ہی میں اور پانی میں بھی مدد کی ہے۔

in_pashto.name: غیاث
in_pashto.meaning: غیاث کېښودیوالی اوبه، اوبه، برسات، برساتوالی اوبه، د ښاګړو اوبه
in_pashto.long_meaning: غیاث کېښودیوالی اوبه، اوبه، برسات، برساتوالی اوبه، د ښاګړو اوبه، دغه نوم د ښاګړو لپاره یو ښه نوم دی، دغه نوم د اوبو سره لیکل کېږي، دغه نوم په افغانستان کې د ښاګړو لپاره ډیر عام دی، دغه نوم د اوبو سره لیکل کېږي، دغه نوم په افغانستان کې د ښاګړو لپاره ډیر عام دی۔

in_english.name: Ghiyath
in_english.meaning: Ghiyath means rain that brings relief, rain, water, shower, downpour, rain that comes after drought
in_english.long_meaning: Ghiyath means rain that brings relief, rain, water, shower, downpour, rain that comes after drought, this name has its root in the Arabic word غيث which means 'rain', 'relief', and 'water', in Islamic tradition, this name is associated with the concept of relief and sustenance, it is also associated with the Prophet Muhammad's companion, Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, who was also known as Ghiyath, this name is considered auspicious and meaningful in Islamic culture, and is often given to boys in Muslim families.

historical_references.reference:
Ghiyath al-Kabir, the great general of the Abbasid Caliphate who led the successful siege of Amul in 716 AD, during the campaign against the Turks.
Context: Ghiyath al-Kabir, whose real name was Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan, was a prominent military commander under the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur. He earned his nickname 'Ghiyath' (support) due to his significant contributions in the military campaigns against the Umayyads and the Turks. In the Battle of Amul, Ghiyath led the Abbasid forces to a decisive victory, securing the northern borders of the Caliphate and ensuring the safety of the Abbasid capital, Baghdad.

Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad ibn Mahmud, the founder of the Ayyubid Empire in 1169 AD, in Egypt.
Context: Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad was a Turkish general under the Seljuk Sultan Amaq, who rebelled against his master and seized the opportunity to establish his own empire, the Ayyubids. He was given the name 'Ghiyath al-Din' (supporting the faith) due to his strong commitment to the Sunni cause and his efforts to unite the Muslim world against the Crusades.
